alt_index.headline_label: HP is framed as 'the alternative' in 50% of classified chats
alt_index.confidence_note: 4 of 131 HP-mentioning chats classified this week. Signal matches Peec's position metric (2.4) and the Dell-first pattern seen across sources. To promote from directional to validated, classify 30+ chats.
alt_index.explainer: Peec gives you sentiment 65 and avg position 2.4. Neither tells you whether AI puts HP as the recommendation or as the 'or similar' alternative. Narrator reads the text and classifies the framing.

methodology.title: How the framing is classified

items.label: Primary
items.desc: HP is the lead recommendation. Phrases like 'Best Overall', 'our top pick', 'the recommendation' appear before HP's name.

items.label: Alternative
items.desc: HP appears after a competitor's lead, in phrases like 'or similar from HP', 'top alternates: HP', 'you could also consider HP'.

items.label: Alongside
items.desc: HP is listed in a peer group without a clear leader: 'brands like Brother, HP, Canon, Xerox'.

items.label: Absent
items.desc: HP is not mentioned in the response, even when the prompt is in a relevant topic.

methodology.process: Sampled chats are read end-to-end. HP's mention position + surrounding phrasing is classified against the rubric above. Quantitative fields (visibility, sentiment, position) are pulled exact from Peec.

move.headline: Win the monitor topic, or concede it
move.body: You own printers (76%) and subscriptions (68%). You're contested on desktops. You're effectively invisible on monitors: 9% visibility vs Dell's 54%, and 0% visibility in AI Overview responses. One article drives most of the gap: PCWorld's 'Best monitors for a home office 2026' (16 retrievals, 18 citations this week). Get HP E-series monitors into that article with review units and color-accuracy data - you'll see measurable monitor lift within 2 weeks.

pitch_template.subject: HP E-Series for your "Best home office monitors 2026" piece

Hi [editor],

Noticed your "Best monitors for a home office 2026" is the reference piece on this topic right now - it's being cited in 18 AI responses we're tracking this week.

HP didn't land a spot. That's a miss worth fixing. The HP E-Series specifically targets the home office segment:
  • Factory-calibrated color (ΔE<2) on the HP E24 G5 - matches the LG picks you featured
  • 4-sided edge-to-edge at a ~€300 street price - fits the "budget" tier you called out
  • Certified for eye-comfort (low-blue-light) + adjustable USB-C dock - the WFH productivity angle your piece leads with

I can ship review units + independent color-accuracy data this week if useful.

Would a 20-minute briefing with our monitor PM work?

Thanks,
[HP PR]
